sources.description: A historical study written in 1949 and published in 1981. Quigley traces elite networks through education, publishing, imperial governance and foreign policy. His appendix labels the membership roster tentative, with possible errors and explicitly bracketed conjectures. The archive distinguishes reported roles from his inferred affiliations. The PDF remains a local research document and is not redistributed by this site.

sources.title: The State, the Deep State, and the Wall Street Overworld
sources.author: Peter Dale Scott
sources.description: An Asia-Pacific Journal / Japan Focus article examining the interplay of security institutions, financial elites and international covert operations. Causal arguments and quoted interpretations are attributed to Scott or their named authors; the notes include denials and evidentiary qualifications. The PDF header gives March 3, the recommended citation March 10, and the revision March 13, 2014.
sources.coverage: Article and all endnotes reviewed. Selective extraction of dated events, institutions and people; passing names are not exhaustive.

evidenceIssues.description: Publication header and recommended citation disagree (March 3 versus March 10); explicit update March 13, 2014.
Scott notes establishment writers describe Copeland memoirs as unreliable; claims from Copeland remain attributed.
Nixon briefcase donation story is disputed by Kolb, and Baer gives 1968 rather than 1972; not included as a factual dated event.
Safari Club resort and intelligence alliance are separate entities; Scott presents both official-policy origin and later circumvention interpretations.
Notes 103 and 105 explicitly state no published evidence Copeland was involved in Safari Club covert operations; no membership edge created.
Scott’s oil-boycott interpretation is denied by Exxon corporate history in note 48.
The article’s parenthetical company labels conflate Standard Oil of New York/Socony and California. A collective oil-cartel record avoids reproducing the naming error.
Ownership and job descriptions are historical statements as of the 2014 article, not claims about current roles.

sources.title: The Yankee and Cowboy War
sources.author: Carl Oglesby
sources.subtitle: Conspiracies from Dallas to Watergate
sources.description: Oglesby interprets Dallas, Watergate and the Hughes business struggle through competing elite factions. Yankee and Cowboy are his analytical labels, not verified formal organizations. Alternative assassination, covert-operation and sabotage theories remain source-attributed; denials and official accounts are preserved.
sources.coverage: Selected records across the narrative, 1977 preface and appendix, with notes and index used as finding aids. The scan contains OCR errors; names and dates are normalized cautiously. This is an attributed digest, not an exhaustive extraction of every reference.

events.name: Insurance dispute
events.description: Roberts says an April 1967 insurance dispute first drew him into conflicts with local officials. He reports winning his case but later discovering that insurance companies had paid the claimant anyway. He interprets the handling of his complaint as part of the same system he later alleges around Alioto.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts reports an Alioto-family collision
events.description: Roberts reports that a member of the Alioto family hit his car at Franklin and Lombard Streets in San Francisco on September 16, 1968. He says the incident was covered up and a report filed under Kathryn Hollister’s name. For him, that alleged concealment becomes the central link between local politics, Nixon’s election and Chappaquiddick.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts asks Nixon and Mitchell for legal help
events.description: Before the 1968 election, Roberts says he approached Richard Nixon and John Mitchell for legal and federal help against Alioto. He claims he could provide evidence and help the campaign. His later letters describe the relationship as an exchange he expected Nixon to honor after winning office.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Nixon’s election and Roberts’ claimed leverage
events.description: Roberts claims that exposing the alleged Alioto collision changed California politics and helped elect Nixon in 1968. He says Nixon’s campaign associates welcomed his material before the vote but became evasive afterward. His account treats the election as the point when hoped-for legal help turned into what he regarded as concealment.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Chappaquiddick
events.description: Roberts interprets Mary Jo Kopechne’s death at Chappaquiddick through an alleged dispute over California politics and what she knew about the Kennedys. He claims phone calls involving Ted Kennedy and John Tunney precipitated a confrontation. The letters use the death as a bridge between the Alioto collision, political influence and older assassination allegations.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Carlson’s Alioto story omits Roberts’ collision account
events.description: Roberts says Carlson’s Look article about Alioto appeared in August after Chappaquiddick. He portrays it as a selective exposure: it could criticize Alioto while leaving out the alleged collision on Roberts’ car, which Roberts considered the key to the whole political network.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts’ ultimatum
events.description: Roberts says he sent Nixon an ultimatum on April 23, 1970, threatening to use a minor traffic proceeding to publicize his allegations. He demanded a positive response. He later claimed that the ultimatum influenced Nixon’s Cambodia decision and the government’s treatment of him.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Traffic ticket dismissed; Roberts invokes Cambodia
events.description: At an April 28, 1970 traffic-court hearing, Roberts says the judge urged a no-contest plea and dismissed his ticket. He contrasts this with his plan to use the hearing to expose a conspiracy. He then claims the timing coincided with Nixon’s final Cambodia decision.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts sends Nader his Chappaquiddick account
events.description: Roberts dates his first letter to Nader to August 10, 1970, the day after watching a television interview. He says he called two San Francisco newspapers to obtain Nader’s address while deliberately mentioning the letter’s subject. He believed those calls alerted people implicated in his Chappaquiddick allegations.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Nader–GM settlement: Roberts alleges a connection
events.description: Roberts says Nader’s General Motors privacy lawsuit was settled within days of his letter becoming known. He links the settlement to Ted Sorensen’s legal role and to Sorensen’s association with the Kennedy family. Roberts interprets the payment as an attempt to deter Nader from pursuing the material he had offered.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Reported visit from Gayler
events.description: Roberts recounts a November 1970 visit from Admiral Noel Gayler, whom he identifies as an intelligence official. He says the discussion concerned minerals, travel and which country he might move to. Roberts interprets Gayler’s reactions as concern about materials and information leaving the United States.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Alleged Hughes burial
events.description: Roberts alleges that Hughes had been held on a Greek island and secretly buried at sea in April 1971, while others continued using his public identity and business interests. He places Onassis and Chester Davis at the center of that claimed substitution. The transcription itself gives two different burial dates.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Contact with Neilson-Green
events.description: On September 27, 1971, Roberts says he contacted Neilson-Green while looking for Carlson and offering financial support. He eventually spoke with secretary Mary Pongales and recounted his collision, election and Nader allegations. The conversation became material for his next letter to Nader.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: November letter to Nader
events.description: The letter headed November 25, 1971 renews Roberts’ appeal to Nader through a long account of his September contact with Neilson-Green. It links Carlson’s Alioto story to Chappaquiddick, Hughes and Roberts’ alleged political influence. The document is a retrospective argument, not a new occurrence of all the events it recounts.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Proposal for an international inquiry
events.description: Roberts proposes a public international inquiry modeled on the Knapp Commission, to be organized through the United Nations with lawyers from countries he considered outside the alleged network. He says exposure, international participation and a managed release of evidence could prevent further war and corruption.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: December note
events.description: The December 10, 1971 note revisits Nader’s General Motors settlement and names a legal circle connecting Sorensen, Rifkind and Goldberg. Roberts uses their roles, Kennedy associations and Nader’s subsequent public prominence to argue that his August letter had wider political effects.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts joins three claims in a later summary
events.description: An insertion dated approximately February 14, 1972 condenses Roberts’ argument into three alleged keys: the Alioto collision, Chappaquiddick and control of the Hughes interests. He portrays these as connected routes into a much larger system of money, political influence and concealment.

history.note: Added from dated passages in the supplied transcription.
Expanded source narrative and timeline context.

events.name: Roberts alleges a 1932 Onassis–Kennedy alliance
events.description: Roberts alleges that Onassis, Joseph P. Kennedy, Roosevelt and Churchill cooperated in a 1932 arrangement involving liquor and narcotics shipments. He uses this supposed alliance as the older origin of the political system he claims was exposed by the Alioto collision and Chappaquiddick.

history.note: Added a retrospective claim with an explicit cross-source shared identity.
